type:
∀ {x κ : ℝ},
  Irrational x → (Roth.approxSet x κ).Finite → ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (p q : ℤ), 0 < q → C / ↑q ^ κ < |x - ↑p / ↑q|
what: For an irrational real x and any real exponent kappa, finiteness of the exceptional approximation pairs gives one positive uniform strict lower-bound constant for all integer numerators and positive integer denominators.
how: Minimize the scaled error over the finite exceptional set augmented by a fixed pair using Set.exists_min_image; take half its minimum and half of one, treating exceptional and nonexceptional pairs separately.
hypotheses: Irrational real and finiteness of the approximation set for the chosen real exponent. The exact captured parameters and existing ambient types are printed; no additional project-defined structure is captured.
caller_summary: 1 explicit source caller declarations, all in LeanEval.lean; 1 direct original value consumers. Exact separate lists retained. Entire LeanEval module proof bodies replay successfully with fresh target name.
mathlib_api_audit: Define the scaled error f(p,q)=abs(x-p/q)*q^kappa. Add the sentinel pair(0,1) to the finite exceptional set and choose a minimum by Set.exists_min_image. Irrationality and positive denominator make that minimum positive. Choose C=min(1/2,f(a)/2). Inside the exceptional set use its finite positive minimum; outside it the failure of approxSet membership gives scaled error at least1, hence strictly greater than C. Lift a positive integer denominator to a natural one before clearing the positive real-power denominator. The sole isDiophantine_iff caller uses this for exponent2+epsilon after ruling out an infinite exceptional set. This is the finite-exception-to-uniform-constant step, not Roth theorem itself.
